transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Mehta (Redwood SE); Omar Ruiz (Redwood Solutions); Marta Alvarez (Ironclad CTO); Samir Patel (Head of Infra); Lina Zhou (Security Engineer); Noah Briggs (Compliance)

Summary (auto): quick architecture walkthrough of private VPC "airlock" concept, data residency controls, KMS/BYOK expectations, and audit log pipeline to SIEM. Discussed firewall design patterns, bastion vs private-control-plane, and regulatory evidence collection for SOC 2/ISO. Agreed next steps for diagrams, pricing, and pilot schedule.

Topics: network isolation, ingress patterns, egress allowlists, KMS/HSM and BYOK, RBAC + SSO/SCIM, audit log forwarding, retention policy, SOC 2 artifacts

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off. quick intros — i'll run the convo then priya will walk the deep architecture.
[00:16] Marta Alvarez: hi yes thanks, excited to get into details — we've got a hard deadline for our audit evidence in q1 so wanna make sure the design fits.
[00:25] Priya Mehta: great — quick caveat, some of the transcript may have misheard product names, but the diagram i'll send will be authoritative.
[00:34] Samir Patel: ok on our side we run a locked down vpc in aws eu-west-1, and anything new needs egress allowlist and justification. we also have an HSM for key custody.
[00:47] Priya Mehta: perfect — that's aligned. high level the private deployment we offer uses a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC, or optionally an on-prem appliance. for your airlock requirement we recommend a two-tier segregation: one for control plane and management, one for inference nodes.
[01:05] Noah Briggs: when you say control plane inside our vpc, do you mean all telemetry and logs flow through our network, or is there a managed component outside? we need answers for SOC 2 scope.
[01:16] Omar Ruiz: good Q — there are two patterns. Mode A: private control plane sits in your VPC with no public egress, all telemetry goes to your SIEM, you manage KMS and keys. Mode B: semi-managed where control plane is customer-side but certain telemetry endpoints upload to Redwood-managed S3 over mutual TLS. both are supported, and we can lock down to Mode A for auditors.
[01:42] Lina Zhou: we need BYOK — our policy forbids third-party key custody. how do you integrate with HSM?
[01:50] Priya Mehta: we support both KMS integrations and HSM-forwarding/BYOK via an external KMS gateway. basically your KMS issues the data key, Redwood never sees the root key. there are a few implementation paths: KMS GRANT flows, or an HSM-backed signing proxy. i'll send sample IAM and grant policies.
[02:13] Samir Patel: and what about host-level hardening? we plan to require our CIS baseline and host-level logging. can we bring our own AMI or images?
[02:24] Priya Mehta: yes, for on-prem and private you can supply approved images. in hosted-dedicated modes we bake in CIS controls — we'll share the SBOM and hardening checklist.
[02:38] Marta Alvarez: about ingress — we only allow inbound from our app subnet via internal load balancer. do you require a bastion for control-plane ops?
[02:48] Jared Kim: we usually recommend a bastion jump host with ephemeral credentials, and session recordings forwarded to your audit logs. for drift remediation we use a customer-controlled bastion + SSM.
[03:03] Lina Zhou: can you support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning for RBAC? we need Role mapping to our groups and auditability of role changes.
[03:12] Priya Mehta: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning is supported. RBAC maps to groups and each API token is tagged. tokens are auditable and we can rotate or revoke via SCIM changes. note: some older docs call it 'SSOC' in auto-transcripts — ignore those.
[03:36] Samir Patel: how do audit logs look? we need to ship them to Splunk and keep 13 months of immutable retention for SOC 2. also need an evidence trail of key rotations.
[03:49] Omar Ruiz: we forward JSON-lines events via HTTPS to your collector or push to S3 in your account for ingestion. retention policies are enforced at your S3 bucket. rotation events are logged with KMS key-id, and we can produce rotation history exports for your auditor.
[04:08] Marta Alvarez: if logs go to your s3, are they encrypted with our KMS?
[04:13] Priya Mehta: yes, for Mode A we write to customer-managed buckets encrypted with your KMS. for Mode B we can still encrypt with your key by using cross-account grants.
[04:24] Lina Zhou: what about egress controls — we cannot allow arbitrary egress to public cloud endpoints. can the nodes be air-gapped and only talk to allowed internal services?
[04:34] Priya Mehta: absolutely. we support strict allowlists: you can restrict egress to internal registries, OIDC provider endpoints, your SIEM, and your artifact repo. for model downloads we can preload artifacts from your internal repo to the nodes.
[04:53] Samir Patel: any need for NAT or SNAT? our security team hates NAT gateways because they're costy, but if absolutely necessary...
[05:01] Omar Ruiz: for fully private deployments you can avoid NAT by using VPC endpoints for required services; we can also host a private artifact registry in your network. NAT is only needed if you must reach public package repos.
[05:17] Jared Kim: quick interjection — we've seen customers prefer a small 'egress proxy' cluster with strict TLS inspection and allowlists; that lets you centralize auditing.
[05:29] Noah Briggs: curious about network policy enforcement between inference nodes and cache storage. are you using security groups or something like Calico?
[05:38] Priya Mehta: we support both — security groups + NACLs for coarse control and optional CNI policy (Calico) for pod-level microsegmentation when running in k8s on-prem.
[05:49] Marta Alvarez: tell us about the control plane API auth — where are tokens stored, and can we force short TTL tokens?
[05:57] Priya Mehta: tokens are ephemeral, stored encrypted using customer KMS. we expose session TTL controls and rotation policies. also support mutual TLS for API calls if you want machine identity instead of bearer tokens.
[06:12] Samir Patel: important: evidence for ISO audits often wants proof of 'separation of duties' and change approvals. do you have change history for config changes?
[06:21] Omar Ruiz: yes, configuration changes are captured in an immutable audit trail (with timestamps, actor, diffs) and we can deliver export bundles for your auditor.
[06:34] Lina Zhou: is there a way to prevent debug endpoints from leaking PII? we have strict data residency and PII controls.
[06:42] Priya Mehta: redwood's runtime supports request-level redaction rules and tokenization. we also recommend prefix-KV caching disabled for sensitive workloads and configure a stricter retention window.
[06:59] Noah Briggs: can you confirm the default retention for logs in your hosted mode and how that differs for private?
[07:08] Priya Mehta: hosted has a short retention by default (30 days) but private mode is configurable to your S3 lifecycle — we typically set 13 months for SOC 2.
[07:20] Marta Alvarez: on data residency — we require all training and inference logs to never leave eu-west-1. can you pin nodes and control plane to region?
[07:29] Omar Ruiz: yes, region pinning is standard for private deployments. we deploy in your VPC subnets only and do not route outside the region.
[07:38] Samir Patel: what about deployment rollouts — can we do canary in our staging vpc first?
[07:45] Priya Mehta: absolutely — you can specify canary subnets and separate keys for staging vs prod. the rollout plan is auditable and you can set automatic rollback on metric regressions.
[07:56] Jared Kim: quick note about pricing tradeoffs — more stringent egress and on-prem images increase engineering time; dedicated reserved capacity costs apply. we'll put that in the pricing doc.
[08:07] Marta Alvarez: fine. for auditors we'll need an architecture diagram, list of controls and evidence for each SOC 2 point — encryption in transit, KMS ownership, RBAC mapping, log retention and export.
[08:20] Priya Mehta: we'll prepare the SOC 2 evidence packet, plus ISO-27001 checklist. i'll include steps for SCIM and SAML mapping and sample assertion tokens.
[08:32] Lina Zhou: what about emergency access or break-glass — how's that handled?
[08:37] Omar Ruiz: we have a policy-driven break-glass flow that requires multiple approvers and writes an immutable justification entry to the audit log; those events are flagged and exported.
[08:51] Noah Briggs: for SIEM integration, which fields do you forward for each event? we need user, action, resource-id, ip, k8s-pod, and request-hash.
[08:59] Priya Mehta: yes we forward a standard schema that includes actor id, resource, action, IP, region, k8s metadata and full event context. we can extend schema to match your Splunk requirements.
[09:13] Samir Patel: clarify network NAT for model fetches again — if we preload models, what's the attack surface?
[09:21] Priya Mehta: preload reduces attack surface because model retrieval happens inside your private network from your artifact repo. otherwise nodes fetch from a signed artifact store over mutual TLS, and artifacts are checksum-verified.
[09:36] Marta Alvarez: any known gotchas with BYOK and HSMs? last vendor we used had delays during key grant rotation.
[09:44] Omar Ruiz: rotation requires short coordination windows: grants must be reconciled by both sides. we can automate grants via IAM scripts and share a rotation playbook to minimize downtime.
[09:58] Jared Kim: let's do a quick run of a sample timeline for pilot: 1) sign SOW and NDAs, 2) share network CIDRs and SIEM endpoints, 3) Redwood delivers architecture artifacts, 4) pilot deploy and run 1 week of throughput and security tests. is that about right?
[10:14] Marta Alvarez: yes that's good — our compliance window wants results before mid-Jan, so need to start early.
[10:21] Priya Mehta: we'll aim to drop artifacts by 2026-12-21 and schedule deployment the week of 2026-12-28.
[10:27] Lina Zhou: one last Q — do you support immutable buckets and object-lock for audit logs?
[10:33] Omar Ruiz: yes, we can configure object-lock on your S3 for WORM retention.
[10:40] Marta Alvarez: perfect. any other risks we should call out?
[10:44] Priya Mehta: the main risk is misconfigured egress allowlists during onboarding — we'll provide a validation checklist and a pre-flight test harness to verify connectivity without opening broad egress.
[10:58] Samir Patel: can we get the pre-flight harness as code or Terraform module?
[11:05] Priya Mehta: yes, we'll share Terraform modules for VPC endpoints, security groups, and IAM grants.
[11:14] Jared Kim: ok wrapping up, we'll collate action items and send the artifacts. thanks everyone.
[11:20] Marta Alvarez: thanks all, appreciate the level of detail.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., 'SSOC' instead of SSO) and some speaker attribution noise; the attached architecture PDF will be final.
